newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lebanese on trial for 10-death German hostel fire.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese on trial for 10-death German hostel fire.

text.p: A young Lebanese refugee was accused in court on Monday of starting a hostel fire that killed 10 people in the worst such disaster to hit asylum-seekers in modern Germany.
Safwan Eid, 21, a hostel resident detained two days after the fire, went on trial in the German port city of Luebeck.
The fire killed six people from Zaire, a man from Benin, a man from Lebanon and a woman from Angola with her six-year-old daughter. Thirtyeight people were injured.
The blaze last January recalled an upsurge of neo-Nazi violence, including firebomb attacks on Turkish homes in Solingen and Moelln, following German unification in 1990.
But authorities later cleared right-wing suspects in this case.
Most of the occupants of the four-storey Luebeck hostel were asylum-seeking refugees from the Middle East and Africa along with ethnic German immigrants from Poland.
Eid, who has been in investigative custody, denies he started the fire and says he is completely innocent.
But prosecutors say he confessed to a member of the rescue team on the night of the blaze. The rescue worker will be chief prosecution witness.

Prosecutors initially brought charges of murder and attempted murder. But these were later changed to aggravated arson and negligent bodily injury which carry a 10-year prison sentence, depending whether Eid is treated as a juvenile which in German law is up to age 21.
Eid's defence lawyer will argue that prosecutors confined their investigations to his client early on and did not focus enough on other possible suspects.
Four youths, including a skinhead from a local far-right group, were detained for questioning, but released after satisfying police that they had genuine alibis.
About 60 witnesses are due to testify in the first ten days of the trial.
